step_1_arrival.title: Arrival essentials
step_1_arrival.whyItMatters: These tasks cannot wait — they unlock everything else.

actions.sin: Apply for your SIN (Social Insurance Number) online at sin-nas.canada.ca (5 business days) or same-day at any Service Canada office. Bring: passport + immigration document.
actions.photocopy: Photocopy all documents ×10: passport, immigration document, IRCC confirmation letter. Store copies separately from originals.
actions.settlement: Find your nearest settlement agency: EMCN (11713 82 St NW), Catholic Social Services, or EISA — all free, no faith requirement.
actions.sim: Get a Canadian SIM card — Koodo, Fido, and Lucky Mobile have affordable prepaid plans.
actions.documents: Understand which documents to always carry vs. keep safe at home.

documents.permit: Work permit / PR card / IRCC letter
documents.address: Proof of address (lease or hotel confirmation)

step_2_ahcip.title: Apply for AHCIP
step_2_ahcip.whyItMatters: Alberta's free public health insurance. No monthly premium. The 3-month waiting period clock starts the day you establish residency — apply immediately.

actions.eligibility: Check eligibility: permanent residents, and temporary residents with work/study permits valid 12+ months all qualify.
actions.apply: Apply online at alberta.ca/ahcip OR in person at any Alberta Registry office.
actions.refugeeNote: If you are a Convention Refugee or Protected Person, the 3-month waiting period is WAIVED — coverage starts immediately.
actions.duringWait: During the wait: access Community Health Centres (sliding scale), U of A School of Dentistry (reduced rates), and the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) if household income under $90,000.
actions.missed: If you miss the 3-month window, your coverage start date is delayed to when your application is processed.

step_3_banking.title: Banking & financial setup
step_3_banking.whyItMatters: A Canadian bank account unlocks direct deposit for government benefits, rent payments, and building credit history.

actions.account: Open a newcomer account: RBC Newcomer Advantage, TD New to Canada, CIBC Smart Account for Newcomers, or Scotiabank StartRight — all offer 0 monthly fees for 12 months.
actions.bring: Bring: passport + immigration document + proof of address. Most banks do not require SIN to open (but add it later).
actions.credit: Apply for a secured credit card — this starts your Canadian credit history. Credit history from home country does not transfer.
actions.cra: Register for CRA (Canada Revenue Agency) My Account at canada.ca/my-cra-account.
actions.remittance: Remittance: compare Wise (low fees), Remitly, and bank wire before sending money internationally.

documents.sin: SIN (add later if not yet received)

step_4_housing.title: Housing & tenant rights
step_4_housing.whyItMatters: Alberta's Residential Tenancies Act protects all tenants — most newcomers do not know their rights until they need them.

actions.clauses: Before signing: check for illegal clauses — landlords cannot charge more than 1 month rent as security deposit, cannot enter without 24h notice, cannot cut utilities.
actions.rights: Know your rights: minimum notice for rent increase is 3 months, eviction requires proper cause and notice.
actions.records: Keep records: document the state of the unit on move-in with photos.
actions.risk: If at risk of homelessness: contact City of Edmonton Housing Relocation Team, FCSS emergency supports, or 211 Alberta.
actions.resources: Rental resources: Edmonton's affordable housing waitlist, Civida housing, EMCN emergency housing referrals.
actions.dispute: Tenant dispute resolution: RTDRS (Residential Tenancy Dispute Resolution Service) — no lawyer needed, low cost.

step_5_employment.title: Employment & credential recognition
step_5_employment.whyItMatters: Credential recognition is the single largest barrier for internationally trained professionals in Alberta.

actions.regulatory: Identify your regulatory body: Nursing → NNAS then CRNA Alberta; Engineering → APEGA; Medicine → AMC then CPSA; Accounting → CPA Alberta; Trades → Alberta AIT.
actions.rights: Know your workplace rights: minimum wage is $15.65/hr, WCB covers workplace injuries from day one, EI requires 420–700 insurable hours before claiming.
actions.wagetheft: Wage theft: file a complaint with Alberta Employment Standards — free, no lawyer needed.
actions.jobs: Job resources: ERIEC (employer-newcomer matching), Bredin Centre, NorQuest trades pathways, Business Link (self-employment).
actions.linkedin: LinkedIn profile: many Edmonton employers screen LinkedIn before interviews.

step_6_language.title: Language & community connection
step_6_language.whyItMatters: LINC is fully funded by IRCC for eligible residents. Community connection is a proven predictor of successful settlement.

actions.linc: Register for LINC: EMCN is Alberta's largest LINC provider; NorQuest College also offers online and hybrid options.
actions.library: Free Edmonton Public Library card: access computers, printing, language learning, and community programs.
actions.events: Newcomer Centre monthly events: peer support, employment info sessions, cultural groups.
actions.programs: Newcomer Centre programs: I-WIN (immigrant women's network), Youth Leading Change (YLC), Global Girls.
actions.volunteer: Volunteer: builds Canadian references and social connections.

documents.status: Proof of immigration status (for LINC eligibility)

step_7_taxes.title: Tax filing & federal benefits
step_7_taxes.whyItMatters: Filing a tax return — even with zero income — activates GST/HST credit, Canada Child Benefit, and other programs. Do not skip this.

actions.file: File your first T1 return even if you had no income. Use TurboTax, Wealthsimple Tax (free), or attend a free community tax clinic.
actions.ccb: Canada Child Benefit (CCB): up to $7,437/yr per child under 6. Apply separately at CRA — do not wait for tax return.
actions.gst: GST/HST credit: quarterly payments for low/moderate income. Activated by filing taxes.
actions.cdcp: Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP): federal dental coverage if no private insurance and household income under $90,000.
actions.provincial: Alberta Seniors Benefit, AISH (disability), FSCD (children with disabilities) — check the eligibility screener.

documents.dates: All immigration dates (entry/exit) for residency calculation

step_8_licence.title: Driver's licence & transportation
step_8_licence.whyItMatters: Alberta accepts many foreign driver's licences for direct exchange — but the process has country-specific rules and a 90-day window.

actions.check: Check your country: about 40 countries qualify for direct licence exchange with no road test.
actions.exchange: Exchange at Alberta Registry: bring foreign licence + passport + proof of Alberta address + fee (~$30).
actions.gdl: If no qualifying licence: graduated licensing — written knowledge test → 12 months Class 7 → road test for Class 5.
actions.transit: ETS Arc card: $100/month unlimited transit pass. Seniors 65+ and youth 6–17 have lower rates.
actions.winter: Winter driving: block heater use, snow tires recommended, how to plug in.

step_9_citizenship.title: Citizenship pathway
step_9_citizenship.whyItMatters: Understanding the path from PR to citizenship helps you plan long-term and track your eligibility clock from day one.

actions.eligibility: Eligibility: 3 of the last 5 years physically present in Canada as a PR. The app tracks your days once you enter your PR date.
actions.language: Language requirement: CLB 4 in English or French. Free test prep resources linked in-app.
actions.test: Knowledge test: based on 'Discover Canada' guide — 20 questions, must score 15+.
actions.apply: Application: online via IRCC portal. Current processing time approximately 12–18 months.
actions.dual: Dual citizenship: Canada allows dual citizenship — check your home country's rules.

documents.travel: Travel history (passport stamps or exit records)
